opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requested admin to Payroll. The notes conflict on employment type: HR indicates full-time Analyst (max write; admin not allowed since Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialists, not Analysts), while Security indicates contractor with basic training (max read). Admin is above the maximum under both interpretations. Granting read is the only level that complies with the most restrictive applicable policy (contractor with basic training limited to read) and is also permissible under the full-time interpretation. Therefore, grant read.
